AFDREV

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
135 AM PST Wed Nov 11 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Dry and mild weather with hazy morning skies continues through 
  Thursday. 

* A Pacific storm will deliver strong winds, valley rain, and 
  mountain snow Friday into Saturday. 

* Additional storms may renew recreation and travel impacts next
  week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

Mild temperatures with dry conditions, light winds, and hazy
mornings continue through Thursday. Afternoon temps may reach near
70 for lower valleys today, otherwise highs in the 60s before 
highs drop 10+ degrees between Thursday and Friday due to an 
incoming storm system. 

This storm system will either bring wind or precip, depending
where you're located. Strong wind gusts in excess of 45 mph will
impact all of W NV and portions of NE CA, including the Surprise 
Valley, on Friday. As of now, there is at least a 40% chance of
gusts exceeding 57 mph in far northern Washoe county and the
Surprise Valley. This has resulted in the issuance of a High Wind
Watch for those areas. Strong winds may impact Mono county Friday,
as well, as the county is under an area of confluence (descending
air) from the upper-level jet streak. For communities along the 
Sierra Front, bursts of wind may precede spillover rain showers. 
Regardless, expect impacts to travel for the Friday PM commute as 
well as for high profile vehicles. Make sure to heed any and all 
travel restrictions issued by NDOT and/or CalTrans. 

Now for the precip. Winter Storm Watches are in effect for the
Tahoe Basin and Mono county from Friday afternoon through Saturday
morning. Rain showers will move into NE CA by Friday afternoon,
reaching the Tahoe Basin ahead of sunset and Mono county by 7-8pm.
Snow levels start above 7500-8000' at the storm's onset, dropping
to near 6000' by midnight (7000' for Mono county). The heaviest 
snowfall rates will occur late Friday night into early Saturday 
morning, with rates reaching 2+"/hr at times. Foothill communities
above 6000' may see light accumulations by Saturday morning. If 
you must travel in and around the Sierra Friday or Saturday, take
the next couple of days to ensure your winter supply kit is "up 
to snuff." This includes, but is not limited to, a shovel, warm 
clothing, tire chains, blankets, water, and snacks. Check road 
conditions as well via CalTrans QuickMap and NVRoads. 

When it's not windy across W NV, expect rain showers from Friday
evening through very early Saturday. Liquid totals range anywhere
from 0.05-0.5" for the Basin and Range (low end) to NE CA (high
end). As of now, there is a 60-80% chance for at least 0.25" of
rain along the Sierra Front by Saturday afternoon. Locations along
the Sierra of NE CA west and north of Lake Davis may see over 1"
of rain; this may produce local ponding on roadways and in typical
poor drainage areas. 

Overall, this is a pretty quick moving system. Showers may linger
along the Sierra through Saturday afternoon, but dry conditions 
are expected areawide by Saturday night. Sunday looks to be mostly
dry before a second system arrives late Sunday night into early 
Monday morning. The details are a bit muddy but snow levels look 
lower, which could bring impacts to the Monday AM commute for 
Sierra communities. 

-Giralte

&&

.AVIATION...

* KRNO: VFR conditions with gusts up to 10-15 kts each afternoon 
  through Thursday. Valley inversions continue each morning into 
  Thursday, reducing slantwise visibilities. 

* Elsewhere: VFR conditions for all terminals with light winds.
  Ridgetop winds are lighter today for all eastern Sierra terminals. 
  Chances for wind shear by around Thur 09Z for KTRK and KTVL.

* For Friday evening into Saturday morning, confidence is increasing 
  for the potential for higher elevation snow above 7,000 to 8,000 
  feet and valley rain showers. This may result in areas of MVFR/IFR 
  in showers, mountain obscurations, low visibilities, and low 
  ceilings. 

* For Friday into Saturday, strong winds may materialize for all 
  local terminals. This could result in areas of mountain waves, 
  turbulence, and low level wind shear.

-McKellar

&&

alerts.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 11 at 10:21AM PST until November 17 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Snow accumulations between 6 and 12
inches above 6,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 6,000 feet.

* WHEN...From Friday afternoon through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions could impact weekend travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches.
